transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m… kind of losing a lot of time checking things. Like locks, work files, notes, even supplies when I’m getting dressed. I keep going back over them, and I don’t really feel like I can move on until I’ve done it enough that I calm down a bit.
Do you have any thoughts that keep repeating in your mind and are difficult to control?

Yeah. It’s usually this thought that I missed something small. Like even if I cleaned a wound area, or checked a CAD file, it keeps coming back that maybe I missed one tiny thing… and then it could turn into an infection or a design mistake that hurts someone. I know I’ve already checked, but it doesn’t really go away when I tell myself that.
Do you feel like you have to perform these checks in a specific way or a certain number of times?

Yeah… sort of. It’s not always a number, but I have to go through the same steps again—like the locks, or file dimensions, or my dressing supplies—until it feels like I can stop. Sometimes that takes… a long time. Hours, honestly.
Are you trying to prevent something bad from happening when you repeat these checks?

Yeah… I think so. It’s like if I don’t check the supplies, or the locks, or the file details again, something could go wrong. I keep repeating the same routine until the anxiety drops enough that I feel like I’m allowed to move on.
Do you feel like these checks are necessary to prevent harm to yourself or others?

Yeah… I guess that’s how it feels. Like if I don’t recheck the dressing supplies, the locks, or the file dimensions and notes, then something bad could happen and it would be on me. I end up losing hours because I don’t feel like I can move on until I’ve gone through it enough times and the anxiety comes down.
Do you get a specific mental picture of something bad happening when you think about not checking these things?

Sometimes, yeah. Not always like a clear picture, but… I’ll imagine I missed some tiny thing. Like the wound area wasn’t really clean enough and it gets infected, or I overlooked something in a CAD file and it turns into a mistake that hurts someone. Even when I know I checked, the thought just… cuts back in, and I can’t really talk myself out of it.
Do you feel like the things you check need to be in a certain order or arranged in a specific way for you to feel okay about moving on?

Yeah… sort of. It’s not so much that things have to look perfect, but I have to go through the same checking routine. Like supplies, locks, file dimensions, revision notes… if I don’t do it in the right sequence or enough times, I don’t feel okay moving on. I can lose hours that way.
Do you feel like the things you check or the way you arrange them need to be symmetrical or exact in any way?

Not really symmetrical, no. It’s more… exact in the sense that I have to recheck the supplies, locks, file dimensions, notes, in the same way enough times before I feel like I can stop. If I don’t, I just feel stuck.
Do you feel like the things you check or the way you do them have to be perfect in any way?

Yeah… perfect in the sense that I have to do it the “right” way. Like checking the dressing stuff, the locks, file dimensions, revision notes. If I don’t go through the same routine enough times, I don’t feel like I’m allowed to move on. I can lose a lot of time to it.
Do you feel like these checks are helping to prevent something bad from happening?

Yeah… I guess so. It feels like if I don’t recheck the supplies or the locks or the files the right number of times, something could be wrong and I’d be responsible. Mostly I keep doing it until the anxiety drops enough that I can move on.
Do you feel like the things you check or the way you arrange them have to be done in a very precise manner?

Yeah… pretty precise. It’s not about arranging things neatly, exactly. It’s more that I have to go through the checks the same way—supplies, locks, file dimensions, notes—until it feels like I’ve done it enough. Otherwise I can’t really move on.
Do you feel like your checking behaviors are motivated by a desire to make things symmetrical or balanced in some way?

Not really symmetry or balance, no. It’s more… I keep rechecking things, like supplies or locks or file details, until I feel like I’ve done the routine enough and the anxiety comes down. Otherwise I just don’t feel allowed to move on.
Do you feel like your checking behaviors are driven by a need to make things exact?

Yeah… exact in the sense that I have to do the checks the same way. Like supplies, locks, file dimensions, revision notes. If I don’t go through the routine enough times, I don’t feel like I can move on. It can take hours sometimes.
Do you think your checking is mostly to prevent mistakes from happening?

Mostly, yeah… I guess it feels like if I don’t recheck the locks, the supplies, the file dimensions or notes, something might be wrong. But it’s also just that I don’t feel allowed to move on until I’ve done the routine enough times and the anxiety drops.
Do you feel like you're trying to control something when you repeat these checks?

Yeah… I think so. It’s like I’m trying to get control over whether I can move on or not. I keep rechecking the supplies, locks, file details… until the anxiety drops enough. It’s not really satisfying, it just eats up hours.
Is your main fear that you will make a mistake if you don't check things repeatedly?

Yeah… that’s probably the main fear. Even when I know I checked it, I get this thought that I missed one small thing — like in a CAD file, or even cleaning a wound — and that it could turn into something serious, like someone getting hurt. I can’t really talk myself out of it.
Is there a specific thought or image that triggers your need to recheck things?

Yeah… it’s usually this thought that I missed one tiny thing. Like even after I cleaned around a wound, or checked a CAD file, I’ll suddenly think, what if I overlooked something and it turns into an infection or a design mistake that hurts someone. I know I already checked, but it doesn’t really… go away just because I tell myself that.
Is your need to recheck things more about preventing a mistake or about feeling in control of the situation?

Mostly preventing a mistake, I guess… but it also feels like I’m not allowed to move on until I’ve checked enough. Like with supplies, locks, dimensions, revision notes — I keep going back through the same routine until the anxiety drops a bit. It can take hours.
Is your need to recheck things driven more by the fear of making a mistake or the need to feel in control?

More the fear of making a mistake, I think. But it turns into this thing where I don’t feel like I’m allowed to stop until I’ve checked the same stuff enough times… supplies, locks, file dimensions, revision notes. Otherwise the anxiety just stays there.
Is your need to recheck things mostly about feeling safe from mistakes or about feeling in control of what happens?

Mostly feeling safe from mistakes, I think. I don’t really feel like I can move on until I’ve checked the same things enough times… supplies, locks, file dimensions, revision notes. It eats up hours sometimes, but it’s like I’m waiting for the anxiety to drop before I’m allowed to stop.
